nodes.description: The aortic media in LDS shows diffuse medial degeneration with elastic fibre fragmentation, extracellular matrix deposition and increased medial collagen. Medial degeneration is more severe with TGFBR2 than with TGFBR1: in one surgical series every TGFBR2 specimen showed grade III cystic medial necrosis and grade III elastic fibre fragmentation, against one grade III cystic medial necrosis among the TGFBR1 specimens. Clinically the weakened wall is stiffer and less distensible; a paediatric echocardiographic cohort found lower distensibility and strain and a higher stiffness index at the annulus, sinotubular junction and ascending aorta in TGFBR2 than in TGFBR1 children.

nodes.description: In cell-based assays LDS-associated TGFBR2 alleles reduce the acute, ligand-induced canonical response: SMAD2 phosphorylation is delayed and TGF-beta-induced transcription falls. The familial thoracic aortic aneurysm allele R460C, by contrast, has a weaker dominant-negative effect with residual signalling, which links the degree of signalling loss to phenotypic severity.

nodes.description: The primary lesion is a heterozygous variant in TGFBR2, which encodes the type II TGF-beta receptor. In the receptor complex the type II receptor phosphorylates specific serine and threonine residues of the type I receptor (TGFBR1) to activate it, so the type II kinase is the entry point of the canonical pathway. Characterised LDS-associated TGFBR2 alleles are missense variants in the intracellular kinase domain that reduce kinase function and exert a dominant-negative effect on the receptor complex.

nodes.description: TGF-beta signalling regulates craniofacial and skeletal development, including cranial suture closure, palatal fusion and vertebral column formation. TGF-beta receptor variants perturb it, producing the craniofacial half of the Loeys-Dietz triad (hypertelorism, bifid uvula or cleft palate), craniosynostosis, and skeletal and connective-tissue features of the spine, chest wall, joints and limbs. Craniofacial features are not a reliable discriminator between TGFBR1 and TGFBR2: in a genotyped paediatric cohort they were present at similar rates in the two groups.

nodes.description: Pregnancy and the postpartum period carry risks of uterine rupture and aortic dissection. In a pooled TGFBR1/TGFBR2 series, 6 of 12 women had a major complication across 21 pregnancies, two of them uterine ruptures.

evidence.snippet: In 21 pregnancies among 12 women with LDS 1/2, 6 women had a major complication either during pregnancy or immediately postpartum, comprised of 4 aortic dissections and 2 uterine ruptures.
